newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH AUDITOR WILL NOT PROBE AGRICULTURE MINISTRY.
newsitem.headline: POLISH AUDITOR WILL NOT PROBE AGRICULTURE MINISTRY.

text.p: Poland's Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK), the government auditing body, refused on Thursday to launch a probe into the Agriculture Ministry's activities surrounding grain imports, NIK said.

The probe was requested by Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko after the government decided on Tuesday to reinstate 10-percent customs duty on most imported grains, which the minister said would hamper his plan to cut inflation this year.
Kolodko asked for an investigation of the Agriculture Ministry-linked food market regulator, the Farm Market Agency (ARR) and intermediary firms involved in grain trade.

Kolodko also asked NIK to investigate the activities of Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski, who has pushed through the cabinet a regulation reintroducing duties on grain imports, which had been set to stay free of duty until mid-1997.
Kolodko suggested that the ministry -- led by Jagielinski, who belongs the co-ruling Polish Peasant Party -- was more keen to protect grains producers than grains product consumers.
But NIK, which monitors operations of government institutions and state-owned companies, said it had already monitored the ARR last year and there was no need for another probe.
"No new circumstances or facts have been put forward to justify undertaking a new, complex probe," NIK said in a statement.
Some agricultural analysts have said the ARR fails to properly intervene on the food market, allowing unexpected price hikes and declines.
Opposition politicians say the PSL has pressed for the reinstatement of duties to ahead of the original end-June target date to boost their chances in this year's parliamentary elections.
